name: tof_severe
title: Tetralogy of Fallot, severe RVOT obstruction on PGE1
description: Term neonate 3.545 kg at 72 h with ToF and severe RVOT obstruction: little antegrade flow, R->L VSD shunt, duct-dependent pulmonary flow; ductus held open on PGE1 (2.5 mm).
grades: A = neonatal ToF primary data/definition; B = infant ToF, textbook figure or fetal; C = derived, interpolated or borrowed from term_neonate_72h

agata1994.cite: Agata Y et al. Pediatr Res 1994;36:805-10 (n=23 term, 2862 g, GA 38 wk; Fig 2 read at 96 h)

arya2014.cite: Arya B et al. Pediatr Cardiol 2014;35:810-6

cousineau2005.cite: Cousineau J et al. Clin Biochem 2005;38:905-7

echo_convention.cite: Doppler RVOT obstruction bands (mild <3 m/s, moderate 3-4 m/s, severe >4 m/s), pedecho.org ToF page

glow2020.cite: Harris DL et al. J Pediatr 2020;223:34-41 (GLOW)

glow2021.cite: Harris DL et al. J Pediatr 2021;231:81-86 (GLOW)

hannover2018.cite: Healthy term neonates during quiet sleep, Hannover. Acta Paediatr 2019;108:231-8

he2011.cite: He SR et al. Chin Med J 2011;124:2284-9

li2023.cite: Li et al. Zhong Nan Da Xue Xue Bao Yi Xue Ban 2023 (RVOT stenting in ToF)

matter2012.cite: Matter et al. Pediatr Cardiol 2012 (ductal stenting in duct-dependent pulmonary blood flow)

norway2021.cite: Heart rate during the first 24 hours in term-born infants. Arch Dis Child Fetal Neonatal Ed 2021;106:489-93

rudolph2009.cite: Rudolph AM. Congenital Diseases of the Heart: Clinical-Physiological Considerations, 3rd ed. Wiley-Blackwell 2009; ch 14 (Figs 14.2-14.4, catheterization section)

satoh2016.cite: Satoh M et al. J Hypertens 2016;34:1578-85

textbook.cite: General neonatal textbook range; no healthy-term primary source found

vanzadelhoff2023.cite: van Zadelhoff AC et al. Br J Anaesth 2023;130:585-94

vetten2025.cite: Vetten Z et al. Prenat Diagn 2025;45:743-51 (PMC12137033)

variables.label: Heart rate
variables.method: oscillometric monitor pulse; mixed sleep/awake (state chosen: calm, mixed)
variables.notes: Borrowed from term_neonate_72h (no ToF-specific neonatal data; compensated-neonate assumption, user decision 2026-10-30). Quiet sleep 112 (87-133, Hannover); resting day 1 120-122 (Norway); USCOM 126 to 120 from day 1 to 3 (He). Mean set between Satoh 117 and He 120. Agata 1994 (echo, n=23): 121 +/- 12 at 24 h, ~120 at 96 h.

variables.label: Systolic BP
variables.notes: Borrowed from term_neonate_72h (no ToF-specific neonatal data; compensated-neonate assumption, user decision 2026-10-30). Read off Fig 4a (GA 39/41 curves interpolated, +/-2 mmHg). Satoh day 3: 70.5 +/- 7.4 (P5-P95 58-83).

variables.label: Diastolic BP
variables.notes: Borrowed from term_neonate_72h (no ToF-specific neonatal data; compensated-neonate assumption, user decision 2026-10-30). Fig 4c. Satoh day 3: 44.3 +/- 6.7 (P5-P95 35-57).

variables.label: Mean arterial pressure
variables.notes: Borrowed from term_neonate_72h (no ToF-specific neonatal data; compensated-neonate assumption, user decision 2026-10-30). Fig 4b. BP still rises steeply between day 2 and 4 at term; exact values via bloodpressure-neonate.com.

variables.label: Right atrial mean pressure
variables.notes: Rudolph: RA mean usually normal (a6 v4 m5 in Figs 14.2-14.4); a wave may rise to 8-10.

variables.label: RV minus LV peak systolic pressure
variables.model_readout: per-beat max RV.pres - per-beat max LV.pres
variables.notes: Non-restrictive VSD: RV and LV systolic pressures identical, square-topped RV contour (Rudolph, catheterization section). Tests that the VSD is non-restrictive.

variables.label: pH
variables.notes: Borrowed from term_neonate_72h (no ToF-specific neonatal data; compensated-neonate assumption, user decision 2026-10-30). Capillary pH ~ arterial pH.

variables.label: pCO2
variables.notes: Borrowed from term_neonate_72h (no ToF-specific neonatal data; compensated-neonate assumption, user decision 2026-10-30). Rudolph: PCO2 usually normal or decreased to ~35 mmHg in cyanotic infants (hyperventilation).

variables.label: Plasma glucose
variables.age: 72 h (between 48 h plateau 3.3 +/- 0.6 and day 4 plateau 4.6 +/- 0.7)
variables.notes: Borrowed from term_neonate_72h (no ToF-specific neonatal data; compensated-neonate assumption, user decision 2026-10-30). Cousineau 48 h whole blood: 3.8 +/- 0.8 (2.1-5.3).

variables.label: Lactate
variables.notes: Borrowed from term_neonate_72h (no ToF-specific neonatal data; compensated-neonate assumption, user decision 2026-10-30). Cousineau capillary whole blood 48 h: 2.6 +/- 0.7 (1.4-4.1). A target of ~1.5-2.0 covers both methods.

variables.label: Hemoglobin
variables.notes: Borrowed from term_neonate_72h (no ToF-specific neonatal data; compensated-neonate assumption, user decision 2026-10-30). Read off Fig 3B; Utah altitude 800-1520 m. Cousineau capillary 20.4 (14.5-23.9).

variables.label: Hematocrit
variables.notes: Borrowed from term_neonate_72h (no ToF-specific neonatal data; compensated-neonate assumption, user decision 2026-10-30). Fig 3A.

variables.label: Core temperature
variables.notes: Borrowed from term_neonate_72h (no ToF-specific neonatal data; compensated-neonate assumption, user decision 2026-10-30).

variables.label: Systemic output (Qs)
variables.model_readout: (LV_AA + RV_AA flow) - ductal Ao->PA flow, per kg
variables.notes: Rudolph: systemic flow usually normal, up to 5-6 L/min/m2 (~1.2 L/min at 0.22 m2) when hypoxaemia is marked. Range borrowed from the term LVO row.

variables.label: RV share of aortic inflow (override)
variables.notes: No quantitative source found. Reported only; RV_AA.r_for is a structural lever.

variables.label: VSD
variables.notes: Large malaligned, non-restrictive by definition; no neonatal mm data. Judged by rv_lv_peak, not by diameter.

variables.label: SpO2 (pre-ductal)
variables.notes: Rudolph Fig 14.3 (newborn, duct patent): aortic 80 %; text: the duct may lift SaO2 to 85-92 %. Li 2023 before RVOT stent 75 +/- 17 %.

variables.label: Mixed venous O2 saturation
variables.notes: Fig 14.3: SVC 55, IVC 60 %.

variables.label: Qp:Qs
variables.notes: Fig 14.3 Fick: (80 - 57)/(96 - 58) = 0.6; a 2.5 mm PGE1 duct gives somewhat more. Rudolph: Qp:Qs down to 0.5 with marked hypoxaemia.

variables.label: PA systolic pressure
variables.notes: Fig 14.3: PA 20/10 m15; low PA pressure with a flat trace when hypoxaemic (Rudolph).

variables.label: PA mean pressure
variables.notes: Fig 14.3: PA 20/10 m15; low PA pressure with a flat trace when hypoxaemic (Rudolph).

variables.label: RVOT peak-to-peak gradient
variables.model_readout: per-beat max RV.pres - per-beat max PA.pres
variables.notes: Reported only: Fig 14.3 RV 85 - PA 20 = 65 at aortic 85, ~55 at our ~74. With a non-restrictive VSD the gradient is capped by systemic pressure and is a poor severity measure here.

variables.label: RVOT peak velocity (derived)
variables.model_readout: sqrt(rvot_grad / 4) (RV_PA is a linear resistor without a Doppler read-out)
variables.notes: Reported only.

variables.label: O2 step-up at RV (RV so2 - svo2)
variables.notes: Fig 14.3: RV 58 = venous 55-60, no L->R step-up.

variables.label: VSD net flow (L->R positive)
variables.notes: Net R->L (negative).

variables.label: Antegrade RVOT flow
variables.notes: Reported: little antegrade flow (antegrade + duct = Qp).

variables.label: Ductal flow (Ao->PA positive)
variables.notes: Ao->PA (positive). Structural: 2.5 mm on PGE1 (user decision; Matter 2012 narrowest pre-stent 1.9 +/- 0.6 mm, length 12.2 mm; ToF ducts are small, Rudolph).

variables.label: Pulmonary valve annulus z-score
variables.notes: Fetal: PGE1-dependent/intervention <= 7 d -5.3 +/- 2.4 (Vetten 2025); duct-dependent -5.38 +/- 2.95 (Arya 2014).

variables.label: SpO2 after duct closure
variables.notes: Fig 14.4 (severe, duct closed): aortic 50 %; rapid closure -> 35-40 %, PO2 20-30, acidaemia (Rudolph). Jo 2018: severe = SpO2 < 70 %.
